analysis:
The only change is documentation: head lines 956-1003 of docs/architecture/inference.md add a startup shape warmup description (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup). The supplied head units cover lines 1-797, so the added text is not visible in the numbered source. I examined the patch excerpt, which is truncated, and the surrounding Nemotron Super, GLM5Next and managed-slot documentation.

Described warmup behavior: a greedy 128-token probe is run twice, then solo and width-N shape cells. They use the artifact's default sampling. A 20 s wall budget applies. The warmup trains no rates or counters and runs once per loaded engine. No code is changed.

Security relevance:
- Warmup prompts are presumably synthetic. The excerpt does not show whether they enter the prefix cache (T-041, SEC-035) under a cache scope, or leave residual KV in GPU memory (T-028). The doc cannot confirm either, and the actual implementation in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift was not supplied.
- The warmup runs on resident engines and consumes GPU time for up to 20 s. This could delay the first coordinator request (availability, T-010/T-029), but it is bounded and preemptible per the doc.
- The doc says no cache receipts or cache capability are emitted for Super. This matches the prior threat-model claims and introduces no new trust assumption.

No security regression is identifiable from documentation alone. Residual questions for the code pass: whether warmup requests are submitted with a nil or unique cache scope so they cannot publish to the SSD prefix cache or be adopted by a tenant, and whether warmup is accounted against the shared KV budget.

The patch excerpt is truncated, so the rest of the added text remains unexamined, and the cache question is not security-material from this evidence alone.
